title: The Most Dangerous Game: inference, evidence and theme
prompt: Read the excerpt, then choose the best answer for each question.

items.stem: "The world is made up of two classes—the hunters and the huntees. Luckily, you and I are hunters." What can you infer about Rainsford from these lines?

choices.text: He feels sure he will always have the power, never be the prey
He secretly fears being hunted himself
choices.misconception: infers a hidden fear, though he laughs and says "Luckily"

choices.text: He agrees with Whitney that the jaguar feels fear
choices.misconception: overlooks his reply that jaguars have "no understanding"

choices.text: He thinks hunting is unfair to animals
choices.misconception: credits Rainsford with Whitney's sympathy for the jaguar

items.stem: Which detail most strongly supports the idea that the sailors fear Ship-Trap Island?

choices.text: "The sea was as flat as a plate-glass window."
choices.misconception: cites a weather detail that says nothing about the crew

choices.text: "Cannibals?" suggested Rainsford.
choices.misconception: cites Rainsford's guess, which is no evidence of the sailors' feelings

choices.text: "It will be light enough in Rio."
choices.misconception: cites a line about their destination, not about the island

choices.text: "Didn't you notice that the crew's nerves seemed a bit jumpy to-day?"

items.stem: Which statement best expresses a theme developed in this excerpt?

choices.text: People who hold power may dismiss the fear and suffering of those weaker than they are
The excerpt is about hunting
choices.misconception: names a topic instead of a statement about life

choices.text: Rainsford and Whitney sail toward Rio on a yacht
choices.misconception: retells the situation instead of stating a theme

choices.text: Sailors are always right about danger
choices.misconception: turns Whitney's "sometimes I think" into an absolute rule

items.stem: Rainsford answers Whitney's story of the "mental chill" with "Pure imagination" and says "One superstitious sailor can taint the whole ship's company with his fear." What can you infer?

choices.text: He believes the dread spreads from person to person, not from anything real about the island
He admits that he feels the chill too
choices.misconception: contradicts his dismissal of the chill as "Pure imagination"

choices.text: He thinks Captain Nielsen should be replaced
choices.misconception: infers a judgment of the captain the text never gives

choices.text: He believes the island is truly evil
choices.misconception: reverses his claim that the dread is imagined

items.stem: Which detail most strongly supports the inference that Rainsford is a skilled hunter?

choices.text: "The best sport in the world," agreed Rainsford.
choices.misconception: cites his enthusiasm, which shows liking, not skill

choices.text: "I'm going to smoke another pipe up on the after deck."
choices.misconception: cites a habit that says nothing about hunting

choices.text: "I've seen you pick off a moose moving in the brown fall bush at four hundred yards"
"Cannibals?" suggested Rainsford.
choices.misconception: cites a guess about the island, not his skill

items.stem: How does the conversation about the jaguar develop a theme of the excerpt?

choices.text: It shows that both men agree animals feel nothing
choices.misconception: misses Whitney's point that jaguars understand fear

choices.text: It is small talk with nothing to do with the story's ideas
choices.misconception: misses how the dialogue introduces the theme

choices.text: It shows Rainsford changing his mind about hunting
choices.misconception: reads a change he never makes; he says "Be a realist"

choices.text: It sets Whitney's sympathy for the hunted against Rainsford's belief that only the hunter matters

items.stem: Taking the whole conversation together, what can you infer about how Whitney differs from Rainsford?

choices.text: Whitney is a braver hunter than Rainsford
choices.misconception: infers bravery no detail supports; Whitney admits "a sudden dread"

choices.text: Whitney is open to fear and feeling, while Rainsford dismisses both
Whitney dislikes hunting and wants to go home
choices.misconception: overlooks Whitney's "Great sport, hunting" and the Amazon plans

choices.text: The two men are enemies
choices.misconception: reads friendly teasing as hostility; they part with "Good-night"

items.stem: Which detail most strongly supports the inference that Whitney himself was uneasy near the island?

choices.text: "Sailors have a curious dread of the place."
choices.misconception: cites the sailors' fear, not Whitney's own

choices.text: "We should have some good hunting up the Amazon."
choices.misconception: cites his plans, which show no unease

choices.text: "Well, I think I'll turn in now, Rainsford."
choices.misconception: cites his bedtime, which shows tiredness, not unease

choices.text: "I did feel something like a sudden chill."

items.stem: Which is the best objective summary of the excerpt?

choices.text: Arrogant Rainsford mocks his kind friend and deserves what is coming.
choices.misconception: adds personal judgment, so the summary is not objective

choices.text: Sailing past a feared island at night, Whitney and Rainsford argue about whether hunted animals feel fear; after Whitney goes to bed, Rainsford hears three gunshots.
Rainsford hears someone fire a gun three times in the dark.
choices.misconception: gives only the last event and leaves out the rest

choices.text: Whitney falls overboard near Ship-Trap Island.
choices.misconception: adds an event that never happens in the excerpt

items.stem: At the end of the excerpt, Rainsford hears a gun fired three times "off to the right." What can the reader infer?

choices.text: Whitney is firing from the deck
choices.misconception: overlooks that Whitney has already gone to bed

choices.text: Rainsford only imagined the sound
choices.misconception: ignores that his expert ears "could not be mistaken"

choices.text: Someone is on or near the island Whitney pointed out to the right
The crew is starting the jaguar hunt
choices.misconception: moves the jaguar hunt planned for the Amazon to this moment
